[4] [5]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: Columbia L 1798 was published no later than 3 March 1928 Documented

Rule 3. The Wanganui Chronicle’s dated review names L 1798, Mengelberg, the Concertgebouw Orchestra and the Adagietto, establishing publication independently of the May 1926 session. The exact first-release date remains unknown; source.rights.published 1928 is a documented upper bound. The recording’s 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension. US status is not established. The selected item’s complete metadata, original-FLAC provenance and disc images disclose no Creative Commons non-commercial licence or separate upstream digital source. No licence is inferred from Mahler’s composition rights.

Mahler, Symphony No. 5, IV. Adagietto — Concertgebouw Orchestra, Willem Mengelberg; May 1926. Columbia L 1798, matrices (W)AX 1548/1549. Original-disc transfer supplied by Internet Archive item willem-mengelberg-cgo-col-l-1798-wax-1548-9-1926; transfer engineer unknown. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US status not established.   4. Yale University Library — Mahler performance practice — Willem Mengelberg section, A Closer Look: 1926 Adagietto, forward pickups, rubato, slower return and coordinated portamento; suggested recording Columbia L1798.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Directive 2011/77/EU — sound-recording term extension — Recitals 1–⁠3 and Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): the extension applies to recordings still protected on 1 November 2013; composition term is addressed in Directive 2006/116/EC Article 1.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
